A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of performative risk minimization for binary variables. Their text, equations, six figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison despite reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original episodic and infinite-horizon RL simulations in Sections 4.2.2 and 5.2. Figure 4 shows the resulting prediction and distribution trajectories; Appendix C documents the algorithms.

after.justification: v2 retains the original RL simulation results in Sections 4.2.2 and 5.2 and Figure 4, with algorithm descriptions in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The linear performative response, squared-error objective, performative estimator, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. The generalized impact metrics added in v2 do not alter these procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic binary-variable settings. The multinomial, independent-group, and nonparametric extensions discussed in v2 are not used in additional training or evaluation.

E2.justification: The naive/RM path and empirical-mean comparator remain in the same comparisons. Newly cited optimization, distribution-steering, and bias-amplification works are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The sampling procedures, sample sizes, horizons, evaluation measures, and simulation algorithms are retained. Figure 4 newly specifies lambda = 0.3 for the existing infinite-horizon simulation; this is additional documentation rather than a changed stated setting.

E4.justification: The existing parameter and sample-size analyses, horizon comparisons, and illustrative drug-efficacy and traffic examples are retained. v2 adds no ablation, robustness test, or evaluated case study.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same one-standard-deviation bands and accompanying uncertainty description. Neither version reports additional simulation seeds, repeated-run counts, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 1–6 preserve their plotted values and trends, including the loss comparisons in Figure 3 and simulation trajectories in Figure 4. No numerical results or experimental findings are added, removed, or revised.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 defines parameter-vector shift, divergence-based distribution shift, and group-and-label conditional bias. These extend the mathematical definitions of impact, while the existing propositions, theorems, derivations, and Appendix B proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contribution statements retain the same scope: analyzing PRM-induced bias and distribution shift for binary variables with linear responses, deriving full-information solutions, and studying partial information through estimators and simulations.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds an interpretation involving probability concentration for multinomial outcomes and discusses extending the analysis to independent groups with predictive covariates. It explicitly identifies group independence as a limitation, potentially plausible for drug efficacy but unsuitable for interacting traffic flows.

D1.justification: v2 adds a replication-repository link and discloses lambda = 0.3 for Figure 4's infinite-horizon simulation. Appendix C.1 corrects 'second period' to 'first period' when identifying uninformative observations, aligning the explanation with the unchanged algorithm.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a distribution-steering discussion distinguishing the work from Kim and Perdomo (2023) and Golowich et al. (2024), plus further performative-learning citations. Appendix A.1 connects the proposed extensions to bias-amplification literature. These broaden context without redefining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and terminology edits, updates affiliation and publication text, and adds an impact statement and Appendix A.1. Former Appendices A.1 and A.2 become A.2 and A.3; the main narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICML typography and reflows the existing figures and text while retaining all six figures and their designs. Figure 4's caption adds lambda values, and Figure 5's caption corrects the bottom row from 'slow' to 'rapid,' consistent with the existing main-text explanation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility documentation through the replication link and missing simulation parameter, and corrects misleading wording in Figure 5 and Appendix C.1. Appendix A.1 and Section 6 clarify possible extensions and their independence limitation. These provide a limited improvement in clarity and usefulness while retaining the core theoretical and simulation evidence.
